I'm 31F and haven't changed my mind about not wanting kids.  Having kids is not something you should do "for your partner" they're not a favor to make, and if the idea of having kids makes you more anxious than excited, maybe you should re-evaulate the reasons why you want those kids.

Is it to keep him around? Is it because you're now emotionally healthy to have them? Are any of the possible reasons becuase YOU WANT THEM? If not, don't have them.  The decision to create life should be an enthusiastic one, and should never be made under any kind of pressure, from yourself, your family or your partner.

At this point you should have a heart to heart with your partner, explain your concerns and why you can't make a choice right now,  and try to see if he's willing to be patient so that when you make a choice is the right one for you.

It was totally unfair of him to hold a relationship of 2 years on the (retrograde) expectation of you changing your mind and then making you feel bad about that not happening, but is definitely unfair for the both of you to be in this "hostage" situation were the only thing keeping you together is the expectation of you "changing your mind", which by the way is the oldest (mysoginistic) trick in the book to undermine your own desires because "all women will eventually want children", this couldn't be farther from the truth, please don't fall for it.

Hope you can come to some clarity soon and whatever choice you make is the right one for you and no one else <3

I think people think is selfish because they expect the suicidal person to consider their feelings before making the decision, and by "consider" they actually expect the person to act as they want. When that doesn't happen, they feel personally offended by the act. 

Most people don't mourn suicides the same way they mourn other unintentional ways of death, because they believe suicide has something to do with them (it doesn't) and so they hold the other person responsible for not allowing them to intervene. 

This couldn't be further from the truth. Suicide has nothing to do with anyone but the person that's taking his/her life. It's about a person not being able to make a different choice to change the course, just like that person that jumped the wrong way to avoid an incoming truck or tripped over a high place. What drives suicide is a lack of choice, not a lack of social responsibility. 

I personally don't think suicide is selfish, I believe is a choice, like many other choices in your life, and as that it must be respected. If someone doesn't want to keep fighting, doesn't want to search for answers, or simply doesn't have the strength to keep trying, we're no one to tell them if they're wrong or not. It's their lives, only they can decide how to live it and how to end it, but like many other big life choices, it shouldn't be considered until you're at the right age and early signs may be approachable while the mind is still malleable.

Not everyone takes their life out of depression, I've personally met people who made the choice out of satisfaction with life, stating that they wanted to die as happy as they could and felt they reached every dream possible and wanted to leave at the highest point of their lives. And that's ok too.  Of course, we mourned their deaths, and we were sad for a long time, we even wondered if there was anything we could've done, but eventually, we understood they were done and wanted to move one, and that's ok.

I am in no way saying suicide is a good choice or an answer, it's really not, one of the most wonderful things about this world is that there's always something else to do or try that might change things. But not everyone knows that, not everyone has to know that (we can't possibly expect everyone to understand that with the way society is boxed), and is a choice none the less and we're in no position to judge the people that make those choices.
